claims.claim_text: The indexed Frantisek Moravec is a high-confidence match to the Czechoslovak career military-intelligence officer František Moravec.
claims.evidence_excerpt: he started to endeavour on intelligence activities
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Official Czech and CIA historical accounts describe the distinctive exact-name officer's interwar military-intelligence career and wartime exile leadership.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on the distinctive exact full name and consistent military-intelligence chronology across the OSS index and two authoritative sources.
claims.temporal_assessment: The sources establish prewar and wartime intelligence assignments but do not date the start or nature of his indexed OSS relationship.
claims.match_notes: The diacritic form František is preserved as a documented variant. The index does not itself state an OSS job title.

claims.claim_text: František Moravec served in the Czechoslovak General Staff's Second Directorate from 1928 as a military intelligence and counterintelligence officer.
claims.evidence_excerpt: assigned to the Second Directorate of the General Staff: Military Intelligence and Counterintelligence
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The CIA historical review dates the assignment to 1928; the Czech Ministry of Defence independently describes his continuing military-intelligence career.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on the distinctive exact name and matching military-intelligence biography.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar military assignment. It is not labeled a civilian employer or asserted as the immediate predecessor to OSS.
claims.match_notes: The later government-in-exile assignment remains distinct; Box 537 review is needed to connect the chronology to the indexed file.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Wesley C Morck is a high-confidence match to Princeton's Wesley C. Morck '25 memorial.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Wes offered his services to the Office of Strategic Services
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The rare exact full name and explicit OSS service align the institutional memorial with the index.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on the rare exact name and explicit Office of Strategic Services service in an authoritative institutional memorial.
claims.temporal_assessment: The memorial sequences business activity before wartime OSS service but does not supply exact transition dates.
claims.match_notes: The memorial supports identity and documented prewar work; the personnel file remains necessary for precise chronology.

claims.claim_text: Wesley C. Morck worked for the Wall Street firm Brinton & Co. after college and before his wartime OSS service.
claims.evidence_excerpt: he joined the firm of Brinton & Co
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Princeton memorial places Morck at Brinton & Co. after college and before its subsequent sentence about wartime OSS service.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on the rare exact name and explicit OSS link in the same institutional memorial.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar employment, not proven to be the immediate predecessor or last civilian employer before OSS.
claims.match_notes: No exact tenure dates or job title are supplied; neither is inferred.

claims.claim_text: Princeton's memorial says Wesley C. Morck acquired a sizeable interest in Clinton Oil Company before his wartime OSS service.
claims.evidence_excerpt: acquired a sizeable interest in the Clinton Oil Co.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The memorial documents an ownership interest but does not say Morck worked for or operated the oil company.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence that the memorial concerns the indexed person; the relationship type itself remains deliberately narrow.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar professional affiliation; exact dates and relationship to OSS entry are not stated.
claims.match_notes: This claim does not qualify Morck for the oil-company employee category because it establishes neither employment nor self-employment.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Theodore A Morde is a high-confidence match to the Theodore A. Morde identified in a scholarly documentary history as an OSS agent.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Report by OSS Agent Theodore A. Morde
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A documentary history identifies an October 1943 report by OSS agent Theodore A. Morde, matching the index's distinctive exact name.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on the distinctive exact full name and explicit OSS designation in a scholarly documentary edition.
claims.temporal_assessment: This establishes wartime OSS identity, not a pre-OSS employer.
claims.match_notes: The personnel file remains necessary to establish his entry date and immediate predecessor affiliation.

claims.claim_text: A contemporary 1940 newspaper described Theodore A. Morde as an explorer associated with New Bedford.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Evening Star's exact-name context identifies Theodore A. Morde as an explorer in 1940; no employer is named.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence when the distinctive exact name is combined with independent scholarly evidence identifying the same name in OSS service.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar occupation. It is not shown to have been his immediate pre-OSS role.
claims.match_notes: Explorer is an occupation, not a named employer or institutional affiliation.
